title: Internal and external
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What drives you from inside, and what do you need from outside?

I said that I want to get to the core of the thought patterns, behaviour patterns and leadership of the person in the book. There is a huge difference between his leadership style and that of the former chief executive of the company he walks into. They couldn't be more opposite extremes.

I said I found it interesting to analyze this not just as culture building in a company but as a parenting style. I broke it down into what is internal, how he thinks and acts, and what is external, how he communicates with people. Or intrinsic and extrinsic: his self-motivation, and getting people to do it for the rewards of getting to the mission.
I said the person creates meaning out of pain, transforming experience into super productivity.

A student said: it was an overbloated corporate structure, with a whole bunch of people not really doing anything productive, stepping all over each other. Another said: the company got away from being a scrappy start-up that had to innovate.
I said: what are the positives and negatives of each style? A student said: the danger of a culture that is ultra-sensitive is that you stop innovating out of fear of stepping on somebody's toes.
Which of the two cultures is closer to yours, and what does it cost you?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write what drives you from inside.
Write what you ask others to do, and for what reward.
Write the culture of your organization in one line.
Write the strength and cost of that culture.
Write how it shows in the way you parent or lead.

check.q: What did I split the leader's personality into?
What did a student say can happen in an ultra-sensitive culture?
choices: You stop innovating out of fear of stepping on toes

check.q: What did I say I wanted to analyze besides company culture?

recap: Know your inside and your outside. Name the strengths and costs of the culture you run.
